- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__delegate_task
tools.description: Needs an agent running inside a T3 thread. Delegate one task to a T3-owned child agent/subagent of THIS thread and run it with only the supplied task prompt, without copying parent conversation history. Choose providers and models from orchestrator_capabilities, which uses the same live catalog as the composer. Prefer native subagent tools for same-provider work only when they support the chosen model and no model options are requested or inherited. Use this for any model missing from the native tool, including same-provider work, for cross-provider work, or for explicitly T3-owned child tasks. For independent T3 delegated review rounds, call delegate_task again with the original brief, prior findings, responses, and unresolved objections in the task prompt. Track each round by its own taskId and use a distinct clientRequestId per round, stable across retries of that round. For a follow-up that needs the same child's conversation, use t3_thread_send on its childThreadId. Set isolation to worktree for a separate checkout based on the parent local commit, with project setup completed before the child starts. Uncommitted edits are not copied; omitted isolation shares the parent checkout. Use delegate_task when model options are requested or the child keeps the parent's provider instance and model with nonempty inheritedOptions from orchestrator_capabilities, even for native-supported models. Native subagents cannot reliably apply T3 model options. Set target.options using advertised IDs: Claude {effort: 'max', fastMode: true}; Codex {reasoningEffort: 'max', serviceTier: 'priority'}. Check providerInstanceId, model, and options in the result. Provider/model and modes inherit unless overridden. Options inherit only for the same instance and model; explicit entries override individual values and [] or {} clears them. A requested runtimeMode must be one the target provider lists in orchestrator_capabilities runtimeModes; an inherited one steps down to the broadest mode it offers. Leave runtimeMode unset unless the user asks for a supervised child: approval-required and auto-accept-edits usually make the child wait for a person at each action that needs approval. Prefer mode='async' for long work; mode='wait' blocks until completion, a blocking question, a pending approval, or timeout. If hasPendingQuestion, pass threadId=childThreadId to t3_pending_request_list, t3_pending_request_read (with requestId) and t3_pending_request_respond, or ask the user; the task's completion still wakes this thread. If pendingApproval is set, read the fresh full request in childThreadId before responding: the record can outlive its provider callback. It grants no approval authority; decisions remain with the child's existing approval holder, and pending request tools answer questions only. The child keeps running and its completion still wakes this thread. timeoutMs on mode=wait is only the parent's wait budget and does not cancel the child. waitTimedOut on that wait call means the timeout fired; keep that taskId and read status on later task_status. An async child's completion wakes this thread through a notification, steered into active turns where supported or queued otherwise, so end the turn instead of polling or spawning watchers; use task_status only when the result is needed mid-turn.

anyOf.description: Model options from orchestrator_capabilities. For the same provider instance and model, overrides individual inherited values; [] or {} clears them. Claude: {effort: 'max', fastMode: true}; Codex: {reasoningEffort: 'max', serviceTier: 'priority'}. Only use options advertised by the selected model.
Defaults to shared: use the parent's checkout. Worktree creates a separate checkout from the parent's current local commit before starting the child. Uncommitted edits are not copied.

Defaults to async. Use wait only when this turn needs the child's result before you can continue. A blocking question or a pending approval in the child ends the wait early with the task still running.

timeoutMs.description: Wait budget for mode=wait only. Default 10 minutes. Elapsing it returns waitTimedOut=true on that call and does not cancel the child.

anyOf.description: Defaults to inherit; omit it unless the user asks for a supervised child. A narrower mode is not a read-only switch: on most providers, approval-required and auto-accept-edits pause the child at each action that needs approval until a person approves it in the child's thread, which this thread cannot do. To limit what the child does, say so in the task. A mode ranked above this thread's is rejected; that ranking does not promise the child's provider permissions are narrower than this thread's.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__html_preview
tools.description: Render an HTML page in T3's headless browser and get back a PNG screenshot, contentHeight (the height the page needs at this width), and its console output: log, info, warning, error, and uncaught exceptions, with stack traces pointing into page.html. console.log is a fine way to report your own checks. Use it to check and iterate on a page before html_render. The first preview on a machine can report that T3 is still installing its preview browser; call again a minute later. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. The page gets the theme variables and layout described in html_render.

anyOf.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels, 240-1600. Defaults to 728, the reply column; use about 390 to check phones.
Theme to preview. Defaults to dark.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__html_render
tools.description: Show a finished HTML page (chart, table, diagram, collage, mockup) inline in this thread, above your final text reply; call it before writing that reply. The reader already sees the page, so the reply should not announce it, say where it is, or restate it: add only what the page doesn't say. Preview with html_preview first. T3 fits the frame to the page's height at each reader's width. On mobile, a height below the page's contentHeight caps the frame there, and the rest scrolls inside it; web and desktop fit the whole page, up to 20000px. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. The frame is borderless on the thread's background, as wide as the reply column (728px on desktop by default, wider if the reader widens chat, about 360px on phones), and its left edge lines up with your reply text. The page sits on the thread's own background, so by default leave html, body, and the outermost element with no background color. This overrides general style preferences such as a fixed black page background. Use a fluid width with no horizontal padding on the outermost element, and no outer card, border, or banner title: the page is part of your reply. If a box needs its own background (a mock of a specific screen, a panel that must stand apart), give it at least 16px of padding on every side and var(--radius) corners, so content never touches its edge. Give charts fixed pixel heights rather than heights that scale with width. Let content set the page's height. The frame grows to fit the page, so a height that follows the viewport makes it grow again and again: html_preview and html_render reject vh, svh, lvh, and dvh units, and height:100% on html or body has the same problem. T3 injects its active theme as CSS custom properties on :root, and they follow the user's theme and light/dark mode live: --background (page background, identical to the thread around the frame), --foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --popover, --popover-foreground, --secondary, --secondary-foreground, --border, --input, --ring, --primary, --primary-foreground (solid buttons), --accent, --accent-foreground (brand accent), --accent-surface, --accent-surface-foreground, --destructive, --destructive-foreground, --destructive-surface, --warning, --warning-foreground, --warning-surface, --success, --success-foreground, --info, --info-foreground, --code-background, --code-foreground, --chart-1 ... --chart-6 (categorical series for charts), --radius, --font-sans, --font-mono. The base stylesheet sets html background/color/font from these, body margin to 0, and hides the page's scrollbar; your own CSS overrides it.

title.description: Short name for the page.

height.description: The frame height in CSS pixels, 80-2000. Use html_preview's contentHeight. A lower height makes long content scroll inside the frame on mobile only.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__orchestrator_capabilities
tools.description: List the V2 provider instances, a short list of their models from the same live catalog as the composer, inherited runtime settings, and app-owned orchestration features available to this caller. The list has the user's favorite and custom models, your own model, every current Codex, Claude, Muse and Grok model, and the first 8 current models of other providers. Other legacy models are left out. omittedModels counts models left out; pass search, such as 'sonnet 4.6', to find them. delegate_task accepts any catalog model, listed or not. For a separate top-level thread in a new or existing worktree, use t3_thread_launch with workspaceStrategy.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_background_wait
tools.description: Keep this thread in the user's Working list and out of their inbox while you wait for background work. Start a background command or Monitor first. Call this before you end your turn if you will act on its result when it wakes you. In taskIds, give the ID shown when the task started. The thread stays in Working until the task ends. The user is not told the work is done. Do not mark work you leave running, such as a dev server or watcher. Unmarked commands and monitors never keep the thread in Working. Pass waiting=false to remove the mark. This does not stop the task. IDs that are not running return in unmatched and change nothing. Only Claude threads support this tool. Other providers return an error.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_read
tools.description: Read durable state and a paginated timeline from any T3 thread in this environment. The default messages view returns user messages, assistant messages, and proposed plans; activity returns all summarized timeline items. Reading an untruncated terminal assistant result from this parent thread's direct app-owned child acknowledges that child's automatic completion delivery. Continue with afterPosition=nextPosition. Recover long item text with itemId and textOffset=nextTextOffset until nextTextOffset is null; offsets count UTF-16 code units. The thread also reports its snooze state and, in pullRequests, every linked pull request; linkedPullRequest is a legacy single link and can be null while pullRequests still has entries. To link a thread for the user, write `[title](t3-thread://v1/<threadId>)` with the threadId exactly as returned, not URL-encoded; T3 Code shows the thread's current title.

limit.description: Maximum timeline items to return, from 1 to 100.

runLimit.description: Maximum recent runs to return, from 1 to 50.

maxCharsPerItem.description: Maximum text characters per item, from 1 to 50000.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_worktree_handoff
tools.description: Needs an agent running inside a T3 thread. Move this agent thread into a new git worktree. To launch a separate agent already bound to a new or existing worktree, use t3_thread_launch with workspaceStrategy instead. Creates the worktree branch (optionally from the base branch's remote), re-points the thread at the worktree, and by default runs the project's setup script there. Changing the workspace detaches the live provider session, so the current turn ends shortly after the handoff is recorded; call this as the last action of the turn. To keep working after the handoff, pass continuationPrompt with the remaining work: it is queued as the thread's next message and starts a new turn inside the worktree with the conversation preserved. Without it the thread stays idle until the next message. The worktree is not removed automatically when the thread is deleted. Fails if the thread is already attached to a worktree.

Save and sync status line: replace the bare SyncDot + "Saved Xs ago" pairing in the status bar with one status line whose words say where the latest words are: "set" (stored on this device), "on the wire" (syncing), "filed" (in the account), "held on this device" (offline/local-only/error with reason). Add <DestinationTag> (computed with loadAiConsequence() or aiConsequenceFor(store.aiSettings) where settings are loaded) to: Get notes, Propose edits, Full analysis, reply send, Ask for a fix, Ask them now / Grade again / Grade this draft (rubric), Send to editor (comments-panel), steering composer in editorial-board-overlay, Apparatus retry. One tag per action group is fine where several buttons sit together; don't clutter. The `.provider-pill` already shows the provider after a run; keep it.
4. The rubric verdict. Bring StampShader back (src/components/rubric/stamp-shader.tsx, a WebGL corona; currently imported nowhere; it was removed from grade-stamp.tsx in commit 0cb77885: `git show 0cb77885 -- src/components/rubric/grade-stamp.tsx` to see how it was wired). Rework it into an ink-impression shader that fits the brand: a short (≤ --dur-ceremony, ~900ms) halftone/ink-spread impression with slight mis-registration of vermilion and cobalt plates, behind/around the grade stamp, played only when a NEW verdict lands (resultFresh / impressionKey changes), never on restore. Requirements: check allowsMotion("ceremony") before creating the WebGL context; canvas ≤ 256 CSS px and render at half device-pixel-ratio; stop and lose the context (WEBGL_lose_context) when done; no loop afterwards; honour theme (read --color-vermilion/--color-cobalt from computed style). Calm level: shorten (use the --dur-ceremony computed value). Still: no shader at all. Also make the existing stamp-die-press keyframes use the platen feel where you can do so in press-room.css without editing global.css (e.g. override animation-timing-function on the relevant class with --ease-platen).

Erase ✕ (permanent, no confirmation today) becomes <HoldToConfirm consequence="erase" label="Erase this comment" hint="hold to erase">. Strike the room (personas clearRoom, also no confirmation) → HoldToConfirm as well.
6. Apparatus (citations-panel.tsx): the deep-trace items that are "searching" get a cobalt reading tick (replace the inline `pulse 1.4s`, mark it data-ambient); when an item becomes "found" it files with a single press-ink-flash in mustard. Bibliography Remove ✕ → HoldToConfirm only if it is permanent (read the code; if it can be re-added from the saved sources, a plain button with an undo is better: say which you chose).
7. EditorialLoader: replace the spinning cobalt ring with a calm set-type line (slugs filling left to right, data-ambient), keeping the rotating wait lines.
8. Editorial Board tabs: the active-tab indicator moves between tabs (a sliding underline using --dur-settle and --ease-set) instead of jumping; unread badges pop once on increment with press-impress (not on every render). Use the paper ink for badge text, not white.

- The manuscript never moves. Nothing you add may shift prose layout.
- Durations/easing only from tokens; no transition: all; no infinite loops except data-ambient ones.
- Every animated state also has a colour or wording cue (for still mode).
- Accessibility: keep aria-live regions, roles and focus management; HoldToConfirm's keyboard path must work.
- Performance: no per-frame JS except the shader during its ceremony; stream updates must not trigger layout thrash (update a CSS custom property, not re-mount).

thread.title: Living press · Lane B · editor chrome

items.text: The drawer, shared arrivals, destination labels, and hold controls are in place. I’m checking the sync state against the actual event semantics now, then I’ll run the requested targeted lint, typecheck, and adjacent tests.

The adjacent tests pass. The first targeted typecheck exposed an existing ambient declaration omitted by the prescribed include list; including the repository’s Mammoth declaration makes that check pass. I’m finishing a second lint/typecheck pass after the accessibility and focus adjustments.

The targeted typecheck now passes, as do the 30 adjacent tests. Lint reports three warnings in existing compositor and workspace keyboard handlers, with no errors. I’m recording the final commit and checking its scope.

Implemented and committed Lane B on branch `t3/living-press-editor-chrome` at **`5e7269c5a56903ebf53b30d1fbbc8fd8495a3446`**. The worktree is clean.

| Ledger row | Built | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Drawer | Width and content transitions, active vermilion tab, and an expanded-state toggle | [index.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1186), [press-chrome.css](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/styles/press-chrome.css:20) |
| Masthead | Marked the wordmark as ambient so the shared motion gates can pause it | [index.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1569) |
| Save and sync | One status line with local, in-flight, filed and held wording; removed the duplicate dots | [sync-indicator.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/components/editor/sync-indicator.tsx:10) |
| Menus and popovers | Shared arrivals and scrim; shortcut dialog uses a fade to avoid movement under keyboard users’ hands | [press-chrome.css](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/styles/press-chrome.css:10), [shortcut-dialog.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/components/editor/shortcut-dialog.tsx:62) |
| Publish and share | Destination tags, published ink treatment, and hold controls for unpublishing, removing collaborators and stopping sharing | [folio-menu.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/components/folio/folio-menu.tsx:1000), [share-dialog.tsx](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/components/collaboration/share-dialog.tsx:557) |
| Zen and flow | Token-based masthead and compositor transitions | [press-chrome.css](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1c307de9/src/styles/press-chrome.css:131) |

I removed the dead `zen-masthead` class usage: the header was already hidden in zen, so its hover strip could not be reached. Unpublishing uses the **erase** consequence because it removes the published record from the current destination. I also added the delayed hydration treatment, sign-in toast styling, and disabled-state styling.

Verification:

- `bun install`, `bun run prompts:compile`, and `bun run i18n:prepare` passed.
- Targeted ESLint passed with three pre-existing keyboard-handler warnings and no errors.
- Targeted TypeScript check passed after adding the existing `src/types/mammoth-browser.d.ts` declaration to the requested temporary include list. The first check without it failed on that missing declaration.
- Adjacent sync indicator, shortcut dialog, and Typst workspace tests passed: **30 tests**.
- `git diff --check` passed. No browser or visual check was run.

The shortcut dialog’s fade-only entrance is the deliberate exception to the requested sliding arrival, following the contract’s keyboard-initiated entrance rule. Zen’s display transition uses `allow-discrete`; its visual behavior has not been browser-verified.

items.text: I’ll inspect the Desk contract and existing implementation, then make the changes within the owned files and run the requested focused checks. I’ll preserve any unrelated work in the checkout.

The Desk currently rebuilds its local and remote views independently, so range changes need a loading boundary as well as cancellation to keep stale requests from replacing newer results. I’m adding that boundary and using value-keyed visual elements so unchanged figures remain in place.

The main interactions are in place: range updates retain the previous ledger, sync events trigger a fresh merge, and the tablist now has keyboard navigation. I’m checking the implementation against the project’s tooling now, including the initial-load and refresh paths.
The focused Desk tests passed. I’m checking the rendered page and keyboard behavior now, then I’ll rerun lint and the targeted typecheck against the final edits before committing.

The browser check confirms the selected range has a distinct ink background, changing ranges leaves the ledger visible, and arrow-key navigation moves focus and opens the matching panel. It also exposed a chart sizing issue; the daily bars now have a full-height baseline to grow from.

Committed Lane D on branch `t3/polish-desk-ledger-motion` at **`378db8978ef9a17a06014f89ddfdfb19218ec417`**. The checkout is clean.

- Targeted TypeScript checking found no remaining errors in the changed files, but failed on the transitive existing missing declaration for `mammoth/mammoth.browser` in `src/utils/exchange.ts`.

Combining them would be better: "set 5s ago" / "filed". I'll restore the age. 2. Text for `savedAt != null` + local-only state → "held on this device · local only". For a signed-out user that's every save, and it's long. Maybe fine but long; the status bar is small. I'll check the visual. 3. `key={filed ? ... : current.kind}` re-mounts the span. OK. 4. Invite with `DestinationTag to="public"`: inviting a collaborator isn't public; it shares with a named person. The contract says "synced, or public if it shares beyond the account". Inviting sends to another person — "public" (vermilion, "Visible to anyone with the link") is inaccurate. I'll override the description, e.g. ``. That's better. 5. Tailwind preflight sets `[hidden]:where(:not([hidden=until-found])) { display: none !important }` in Tailwind v4. `!important` would prevent the display transition from working (display stays none immediately), so the exit animation won't play; the entry via `@starting-style` will work. The doc says flow "eases out as one sheet"; the original 1.2s slow fade was deliberate ("chrome fades over 1.2s"). Lane B made the desk controls fade in 320ms while the header still fades in 1.2s — inconsistent. Each surface has one idea that belongs to a press room: what it is, and what it tells the writer. Everything listed here has shipped. Where a row was checked only through its CSS and component code, not live end to end (because it needs a signed-in account or a streaming model), the row says so.

### The manuscript

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Typing | **Wet ink.** Words set by hand sit in a bluer, wetter ink until IndexedDB has the draft, pass through a drying tone, then are just ink ([`extensions/wet-ink.ts`](../../src/components/editor/extensions/wet-ink.ts)). Painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so there is no DOM, layout or transform. Pastes, undo, drops and collaborators' edits arrive dry. | Your words are safe once they dry. Ink that stays wet means the save has not landed. |
| Caret | A vermilion caret, the editor's pencil. It never glides: Word's smoothed caret is the cautionary tale. | Where the hand is, instantly. |
| Selection | Non-photo blue, the copy editor's proof pencil, instead of the system highlight. | A marked passage, ready for a decision. |
| Selection toolbar | It slides up off the line once per new passage (a Web Animation on `translate`, so the toolbar is never re-mounted). Find sources and Ask an editor carry a docket mark in their destination ink, read from the writer's saved AI and Apparatus settings. | Before you press: what stays here and what is read by a model, and whose. |
| Section drag | The ⋮⋮ handle is a type slug that lights when its heading is hovered. The drag image is the section's heading on a slug. The drop target is a vermilion composing rule reading "set *Section* here". | Moving a section is moving set type: the whole block goes. |
| File drop | A docket that says where the plate will live: inline on this device when offline, your account's image storage when signed in, or that sign-in is needed. | Where the image goes, before you let go. |
| Moving the mouse | **The desk lamp.** A pool of light on the desk around the sheet ([`desk-lamp.ts`](../../src/components/editor/desk-lamp.ts)). It sits where the hour puts it (morning light from the left, evening from the right, warm at the day's ends) and leans toward the pointer when you are not typing. It is painted behind the page, so prose contrast never changes. | The room is lit and inhabited, and quiet while you write. |
| Scrolling | The lamp is fixed to the desk, so the paper slides under it. **The running foot**: the status bar names the section being read, set again from below as you cross into the next one ([`running-foot.ts`](../../src/components/editor/running-foot.ts)). Pressing it returns to that heading. | Where you are in a long manuscript, without a single line of prose moving. |

### The editor chrome

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Drawer | The active folio wears a vermilion tab that slips in on switch. The drawer's contents slide with it instead of being clipped. The toggle takes the editorial ink while the drawer is out. | Which manuscript is on the desk. |
| Masthead | The wordmark's hand-set wobble is ambient: it rests while you type, in flow, and below the full level. | A press at rest versus a press at work. |
| Save and sync | One line: "Saved 4s ago · held here / on the wire / filed", the route word in its consequence ink. "Filed" flashes once when the account has the words. | Exactly where the latest words are. |
| Menus and popovers | One arrival everywhere (File, account, sharing, compositor pickers, Typst status, shortcuts), and one scrim. | A menu belongs to what opened it. |
| Export | One "device" docket for the whole Export group. | Exports are files written here; nothing is sent. |
| Publish and share | Publish, PDS and Micropub carry the public docket and ink across when they succeed. Invite carries "invitee" (one named reader, not the public). Unpublish, Unpublish from PDS, removing a collaborator and Stop sharing are holds. *Checked by CSS and component only: needs a signed-in account.* | Public actions look public; permanent ones resist a slip. |
| Opening the editor | The "Setting the type…" gate waits 150 ms before it shows, so fast loads never flash it, and sets a line of slugs while it waits. | Work is happening, without a spinner. |
| Zen and flow | Zen eases the masthead and compositor out together. Flow keeps the global 1.2 s fade, because leaving for flow is ambient, not feedback. | The room steps back as a whole when you write. |

### The writers' room

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| An editor reading | A pencil ring on the editor's portrait, tied to the real stream: reasoning traces a third of the ring, writing advances it with the characters received, and filing closes it. A faint shared mark shows while the background room is reading. *Checked by CSS and component only: needs a streaming model.* | Who is reading your draft now, and how far they have got. No spinner. |
| A note arriving | Filed notes slip onto the board, staggered at most 50 ms (capped at six). A note that has just been filed takes one ink impression in its editor's colour. A finished reply settles once. *Component only.* | Something new is on the board, and from whom. |
| Asking the room | One "The draft goes to · model / credit" docket under Get notes, Propose edits and Full analysis. Smaller dockets on reply, Ask for a fix, Send to editor, steering, the rubric's grade keys and Apparatus retry. | Whose model reads this, and whether it spends credit. |
| The verdict | **Ink squeezed from under the die.** At the moment the walnut die lands, a halftone in the grade's own ink is pushed out past the sunburst's rays, with a vermilion second plate a hair out of register. It spreads, holds and dries away within `--dur-ceremony`, and then the WebGL context is surrendered ([`stamp-shader.tsx`](../../src/components/rubric/stamp-shader.tsx)). It never plays on restore and never at still. The die itself now lands on the platen curve. | The judgement is in, and it is weighty. |
| Marginalia | Striking a comment rules a line through it. Erasing a comment, striking the room and removing a source are holds. | Settled versus gone. |
| Apparatus | A source being searched carries a cobalt reading tick (ambient). A found source files with one mustard flash. | Research is happening, and something was found. |
| Waiting | The editorial loader sets a line of slugs instead of spinning a ring. Its rotating wait lines stay. | A long wait, in the room's own terms. |
| Board tabs | The active underline slides between tabs. Unread badges press in once, only when the count rises. | Where you are, and what is new. |

### My Desk

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Opening the ledger | Figures are set like a composing stick: numerals roll into place once and re-set only when that figure changes. Readers get the whole value, never the digits. | A dossier being prepared for you. |
| Range | Switching keeps the old figures on the page, dimmed and `aria-busy`, and re-sets only what changed. The selected range is visibly inked (it showed only in `aria-pressed` before). | The same desk, through a different window of time. |
| Heatmap | Cells have a hover state and press when chosen. The selected-day aside slides in like a ledger page. | Which day you are reading. |
| Charts | Bars rise from the baseline once, on arrival or when their values change, and fills grow from the left. | Activity accumulating, not decoration. |
| Patterns | A pattern that crosses its evidence threshold gets a small *filed* stamp, once per device. | Evidence has accumulated. |
| Hosted charges | Money is printed in the credit ink under a credit docket. | This is the part that costs. |
| Tables and tabs | Data tables open with a turning marker. Usage tabs slide their indicator, crossfade their panel, and are a full keyboard tablist. | Ordinary controls, set in the house manner. |

'''
s = s[:start] + ledger + s[end:]

old_perf = s[s.index("## Performance contract"):s.index("## Adding to it")]
new_perf = '''## Performance contract

- Nothing new runs per keystroke beyond `markTyping()` (a timer reset) and, for wet ink, one range append per transaction, painted at most once a frame.
- The save path (`twyne:draft-saved`) drives drying, so drying costs nothing while the writer is typing.
- The running foot measures headings after the debounced `twyne:content` event. A scroll frame reads `scrollTop` and walks a cached list.
- The only shader is the verdict's. It runs on a canvas about 1.6× the stamp (never over 256 CSS px) for one ceremony, then loses its context. Nothing renders behind the manuscript on a loop.
- The desk lamp is a CSS gradient on two registered properties. They are written at most once a frame while the pointer moves, and once a minute for the hour.
- `bun run test:typing` is the arbiter. A change that moves its numbers is a regression, whatever it looks like.

'''
s = s.replace(old_perf, new_perf, 1)
p.write_text(s)
print("ok")
EOF

Typing: wet ink that dries when it's saved

The same sentence, typed and then saved. Before, nothing changes. After, new words stay in a bluer ink until IndexedDB has the draft, then dry to black. If the ink stays wet, the save hasn't landed.

Why: the caret and the text are the most frequent thing in the app, so the budget is colour only. Nothing moves or reflows. The ink is painted with the Custom Highlight API, which adds no DOM nodes. The caret is vermilion and never glides (Word's smooth caret makes typing feel late), and the selection is a copy editor's non-photo blue.

Where the words are

The status bar used to show a grey dot. It now says where the latest words are, in that destination's ink: "held here" (hollow, this device), "on the wire", then "filed" in the account's green.

Selecting: every ask says where the passage goes

The toolbar now slides up off the line once per new passage. Find sources and Ask an editor carry a docket dot in their destination's ink, read from your saved settings: mustard when a hosted model reads it and spends credit, cobalt when it's your own model. Comment stays on the device.

Moving the mouse: the desk lamp

A pool of warm light on the desk around the page. It sits where the hour puts it (from the left in the morning, from the right in the evening, warmer at the ends of the day) and leans toward the hand while you aren't typing. It never lights the page itself, so the text's contrast never changes. Broadsheet keeps it off; it rests while you type and below the Full level.

Scrolling: a running foot, and paper sliding under the lamp

The status bar names the section you're reading, like a chapter title at the foot of a book page. The name is set again as you scroll into the next section, and pressing it takes you back to that heading. The lamp stays fixed to the desk, so the paper slides under it.

Dragging: set type, and a docket that says where an image will live

A section's handle is now a type slug. The drop target is a vermilion composing rule that names what's moving. A file dragged in shows a docket saying where the image would be stored: inline on this device when offline, in your account's storage when signed in, or that you need to sign in.

Losing something for good: hold to confirm

Erasing a comment used to be a single unguarded click. Now a quick click erases nothing and shows a "hold to erase" slip; holding the key fills it with ink and erases at the end. Keyboard users press Enter twice. The same guard covers striking the room, removing a source, Stop sharing, removing a collaborator and both Unpublish actions.

Found and fixed while verifying: the first version erased a comment about a second after a plain click. Qwik's handler for the press ran after the release, so the hold never got cancelled. The press is now tracked with native listeners, and a browser test confirms a quick click erases nothing.

The verdict: ink squeezed out from under the stamp

When a new grade lands, a halftone of the grade's own ink is pushed out past the stamp's rays at the moment the wooden die hits. A vermilion second plate sits slightly out of register. It dries away within 0.9s and the WebGL context is then released. It never plays on a restored grade or at the Still level. The shader existed but was imported nowhere before.

The writers' room

The room's three asks share one line saying where the draft goes. The tab underline slides, and Clear became a hold. An editor's portrait shows a reading ring that follows the real stream instead of a spinning ✦.

The reading ring, note arrivals and the per-editor ink impression need a streaming model to see live. They were checked through their components and CSS, not end to end.

Chrome

The File menu now carries a single "device" docket on Export, since exports are files written to this device and nothing is sent anywhere. The active folio in the drawer wears a vermilion tab, and the drawer toggle turns vermilion while it's open.

My Desk

Figures roll into place once when the page opens, and bars rise once. Picking a day presses its cell. Patterns that pass their evidence threshold get a filed stamp the first time. Two bugs fixed: the selected range was invisible, and switching range flashed the loader.

The rules behind all of it

RuleWhat it means in practice
The manuscript never movesNothing animates prose position or layout. Ink may change colour; everything else moves around the page.
Frequency sets the budgetKeystrokes: colour only. Presses: ≤ 120 ms. Arrivals: ≤ 320 ms. Ceremonies such as a verdict or a publish: up to 900 ms.
One ink per destinationdevice · account · your model · hosted credit · public · erased. Always with a word, never colour alone.
Ambient life restsThe lamp, the masthead wobble and the room's listening mark pause while you type, during flow, and below Full.
Still is stillA Motion setting (System / Full / Calm / Still) is applied before first paint. Still stops all movement; state still shows through colour and words.

The full vocabulary sheet (inks, hold states, ring, slugs, springs, durations) is at artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/page/specimen.webp, and the contract is docs/design/living-press.md.

input.title: The living press: before and after
input.html:
Typing: wet ink that dries when it's saved

The same sentence, typed and then saved. Before, nothing changes. After, new words stay in a bluer ink until IndexedDB has the draft, then dry to black. If the ink stays wet, the save hasn't landed.

Why: the caret and the text are the most frequent thing in the app, so the budget is colour only. Nothing moves or reflows. The ink is painted with the Custom Highlight API, which adds no DOM nodes. The caret is vermilion and never glides (Word's smooth caret makes typing feel late), and the selection is a copy editor's non-photo blue.

Where the words are

The status bar used to show a grey dot. It now says where the latest words are, in that destination's ink: "held here" (hollow, this device), "on the wire", then "filed" in the account's green.

Selecting: every ask says where the passage goes

The toolbar now slides up off the line once per new passage. Find sources and Ask an editor carry a docket dot in their destination's ink, read from your saved settings: mustard when a hosted model reads it and spends credit, cobalt when it's your own model. Comment stays on the device.

Moving the mouse: the desk lamp

A pool of warm light on the desk around the page. It sits where the hour puts it (from the left in the morning, from the right in the evening, warmer at the ends of the day) and leans toward the hand while you aren't typing. It never lights the page itself, so the text's contrast never changes. Broadsheet keeps it off; it rests while you type and below the Full level.

Scrolling: a running foot, and paper sliding under the lamp

The status bar names the section you're reading, like a chapter title at the foot of a book page. The name is set again as you scroll into the next section, and pressing it takes you back to that heading. The lamp stays fixed to the desk, so the paper slides under it.

Dragging: set type, and a docket that says where an image will live

A section's handle is now a type slug. The drop target is a vermilion composing rule that names what's moving. A file dragged in shows a docket saying where the image would be stored: inline on this device when offline, in your account's storage when signed in, or that you need to sign in.

Losing something for good: hold to confirm

Erasing a comment used to be a single unguarded click. Now a quick click erases nothing and shows a "hold to erase" slip; holding the key fills it with ink and erases at the end. Keyboard users press Enter twice. The same guard covers striking the room, removing a source, Stop sharing, removing a collaborator and both Unpublish actions.

Found and fixed while verifying: the first version erased a comment about a second after a plain click. Qwik's handler for the press ran after the release, so the hold never got cancelled. The press is now tracked with native listeners, and a browser test confirms a quick click erases nothing.

The verdict: ink squeezed out from under the stamp

When a new grade lands, a halftone of the grade's own ink is pushed out past the stamp's rays at the moment the wooden die hits. A vermilion second plate sits slightly out of register. It dries away within 0.9s and the WebGL context is then released. It never plays on a restored grade or at the Still level. The shader existed but was imported nowhere before.

The writers' room

The room's three asks share one line saying where the draft goes. The tab underline slides, and Clear became a hold. An editor's portrait shows a reading ring that follows the real stream instead of a spinning ✦.

The reading ring, note arrivals and the per-editor ink impression need a streaming model to see live. They were checked through their components and CSS, not end to end.

Chrome

The File menu now carries a single "device" docket on Export, since exports are files written to this device and nothing is sent anywhere. The active folio in the drawer wears a vermilion tab, and the drawer toggle turns vermilion while it's open.

My Desk

Figures roll into place once when the page opens, and bars rise once. Picking a day presses its cell. Patterns that pass their evidence threshold get a filed stamp the first time. Two bugs fixed: the selected range was invisible, and switching range flashed the loader.

The rules behind all of it

RuleWhat it means in practice
The manuscript never movesNothing animates prose position or layout. Ink may change colour; everything else moves around the page.
Frequency sets the budgetKeystrokes: colour only. Presses: ≤ 120 ms. Arrivals: ≤ 320 ms. Ceremonies such as a verdict or a publish: up to 900 ms.
One ink per destinationdevice · account · your model · hosted credit · public · erased. Always with a word, never colour alone.
Ambient life restsThe lamp, the masthead wobble and the room's listening mark pause while you type, during flow, and below Full.
Still is stillA Motion setting (System / Full / Calm / Still) is applied before first paint. Still stops all movement; state still shows through colour and words.

The full vocabulary sheet (inks, hold states, ring, slugs, springs, durations) is at artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/page/specimen.webp, and the contract is docs/design/living-press.md.

0.23.2.md
====
# Deploying Twyne

Twyne ships as a Qwik City SSR app. The browser bundle is built by Vite into
`dist/`, the SSR server entry into `server/`, and `server.js` (Node `http`)
serves both and listens on `$PORT`.

## Railway (primary)

The repo is configured for [Railway](https://railway.com) via `railway.json`
(`builder: RAILPACK`) and [`railpack.json`](https://railpack.com) — Railpack is
Railway's successor to Nixpacks:

- **Install** (Bun): `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- **Build** (Bun): `bash scripts/railway-build.sh` — runs Convex deploy + Vite
  client + Vite SSR server. If `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is unset, the script
  degrades to a frontend-only build (backend left untouched).
- **Start** (Node): `node server.js`
- **Healthcheck**: `GET /`

> The `build` step is auto-generated by Railpack from the Node provider
> (uses the mise step to install `bun` + `node`, then runs
> `bun install --frozen-lockfile`). We only override the `build` step to
> inject the Convex deploy + Vite build via `scripts/railway-build.sh` —
> the script is required because the inline `if/then/else` with nested
> single-quoted `&&` strings gets mangled by the build step's shell
> serialization.

`railpack.json` pins `node: 20` + `bun: 1` so the runtime image has `node`
available for the start command (`server.js` uses `node:http`), while Bun does
the install and Vite build.

### One-time setup

1. **Create / link the service** (already linked to `Diogenesoftoronto/twyne`):

   ```bash
   railway add --service twyne --repo Diogenesoftoronto/twyne
   ```

   Railway auto-deploys on every push to the connected branch.

2. **Set environment variables** (see `.env.example` for the full list). The
   `VITE_*` values are baked in at build time, so they must be set on the
   service before the first build:

   ```bash
   railway variables \
     --set "CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=prod:your-deployment|..." \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.cloud" \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_SITE_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.site" \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=..." \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://www.twyne.love" \
     --set "SITE_URL=https://www.twyne.love"
   ```

   `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is the production **deploy key** from the Convex
   dashboard (Settings → Deploy keys). The build step uses it to push the
   backend; without it the build only ships the frontend. `PORT` is injected by
   Railway automatically — do not set it.

3. **Custom domain**: in the Railway service → Settings → Networking, add
   `www.twyne.love` and point the DNS `CNAME` at the generated Railway target.
   Until the domain resolves, auth callbacks that expect `https://www.twyne.love`
   will not complete — use the `*.up.railway.app` URL or temporarily set
   `BETTER_AUTH_URL`/`SITE_URL` to it while testing.

### Convex in production

`VITE_CONVEX_URL` should point at a **production** Convex deployment, not a dev
one. The Railway build now runs `npx convex deploy` (gated on `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY`)
as part of the build step, so the backend deploys on every push alongside the
frontend — no separate manual deploy needed.

Sign-in is through Not Organic. ATProto is a separate publishing connection;
Twyne’s email-code and passkey routes are retired. Register each public sign-in
origin with Not Organic, including its `/auth/notorganic/` callback.

Server-side Convex secrets (`NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY`,
`NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_KEY_ID`, `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED`,
`NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED`, `POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY`,
`RESEND_API_KEY`, `VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) live in the Convex deployment's
own environment, not Railway. Set them against production from the CLI:

```bash
npx convex env set NOTORGANIC_ENABLED true --prod
npx convex env set NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED true --prod
npx convex env set POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY phc_xxx --prod
npx convex env set VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY sk_xxx --prod
# list / verify:
npx convex env list --prod
```

## Feature flags

Two capabilities ship dark and are switched on through PostHog feature flags
(runtime, per user/environment):

| Flag             | Effect                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `twyne-pricing`  | Enables the `/pricing` page (Not Organic checkout with Paddle payment processing) + its nav links. Off ⇒ direct visits redirect home after flags load. |
| `twyne-local-ai` | Surfaces the desktop-only native LiteRT-LM model (OpenBMB MiniCPM5-2B) in the UI.                                                                      |

Set `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and optionally `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST`
(`https://us.i.posthog.com` by default) in the frontend deployment. The legacy
`PUBLIC_FEATURE_PRICING` and `PUBLIC_FEATURE_LOCAL_AI` env vars are fallback
defaults for local/offline builds where PostHog is absent; PostHog should own
production rollout.

Firefox (including Android and iOS) skips the browser PostHog SDK entirely:
no analytics, session replay, surveys, or remote feature-flag requests. It
uses the `PUBLIC_FEATURE_*` fallback values regardless of the user's location.
Server-side PostHog capture remains configured separately.

In other browsers, PostHog starts when the document is idle, with a 1.5-second
SDK-load deadline. Blocked or failed initialization is skipped for the rest of
the page session. Analytics and identity lookups never wait for SDK loading before an
app action continues. Feature flags start ready with the fallback values;
failed refreshes preserve the current values, and unchanged values do not
trigger UI updates.

PostHog also captures AI Observability events for evals. Browser-side BYOK and
desktop-local model calls emit `$ai_generation` through `posthog-js`; Convex
server-side hosted AI calls emit the same event via the capture API when
`POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY` (and optional `POSTHOG_HOST`) is set in Convex. Create
PostHog evals against `$ai_generation`, then filter/break down by
`twyne_feature`, `$ai_provider`, `$ai_model`, `twyne_persona_id`, and
`twyne_expected_format`.

**Not Organic and Paddle** (when pricing is on): set
`NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true`, configure the server-held assertion key pair
(`NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY` and `NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_KEY_ID`), and set
`NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED=true` after the `twyne_pro_v2` plan is mapped
in Not Organic. Not Organic owns the product checkout and wallet state; Paddle
handles payment processing. Twyne entitlement is read from Not Organic wallet and plan state.

**Hosted voice** (Pro tier): set `VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY` in Convex, optionally
`VOICE_OPENAI_MODEL` (defaults to `gpt-4o-mini-tts`) and `VOICE_OPENAI_VOICE`
(defaults to `alloy`). If `VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset, hosted voice uses
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. BYOK voice does not use server secrets.

  degrades to a frontend-only build (backend left untouched).

- **Healthcheck**: `GET /`

> `bun install --frozen-lockfile`). We only override the `build` step to
> inject the Convex deploy + Vite build via `scripts/railway-build.sh` —

> single-quoted `&&` strings gets mangled by the build step's shell
> serialization.

== railway-build.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Railway build step: deploy Convex backend (when key is configured), then
# build the Qwik City frontend + SSR server.
#
# Gating: when CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY is unset (frontend-only deploys, preview
# environments, local re-runs) we still build the frontend but skip the
# backend push.

set -euo pipefail

if [ -n "${CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "==> Deploying Convex backend"
  # 1.46 fixes index-removal review with deploy-only keys. Keep CI deployment
  # tooling explicit even when the app's lockfile pins an older client.
  npx --yes convex@1.46.0 deploy --cmd 'bun run build.client && bun run build.server'
else
  echo "==> CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY not set — building frontend only, skipping convex deploy"
  bun run build.client
  bun run build.server
fi
== railway.json
{
  "$schema": "https://railway.com/railway.schema.json",
  "build": {
    "builder": "RAILPACK"
  },
  "deploy": {
    "startCommand": "node server.js",
    "healthcheckPath": "/",
    "healthcheckTimeout": 120,
    "restartPolicyType": "ON_FAILURE",
    "restartPolicyMaxRetries": 5
  }
}
== bunfig
[install]
# Keep Twyne's existing dependency layout when adding the local adapter workspace.
linker = "hoisted"

description: User wants heavy parallel Terra swarms and is fine with E2B/Railway/Cloudflare sandboxes for compute; local disk/RAM is not a reason to serialize

The user wants me to use Terra subagent swarms "as much as you can". They are fine with offloading compute to remote sandboxes, not just this machine: "u can work with e2b and railway and cloudflare sandboxes dude" (2026-10-28).

**Why:** this machine has about 55 GB free disk and 31 GB RAM, and each `desktop/gpui` ui-tests build takes about 12 GB. When I limited lane count to fit the local machine, the user pushed back.

**How to apply:**
- Fan work out to many parallel `delegate_task` lanes ([[model-nicknames-for-delegation]]).
- Put heavy builds and captures on remote sandboxes.
- Credentials (never print them):
  - E2B: `e2b_api_key@secrets` (retired for builds; see below).
  - Cloudflare: `cloudflare@secrets` plus `cloudflare_account_id@default`.
  - Railway: the CLI is already logged in.

== railway-build.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Railway build step: deploy Convex backend (when key is configured), then
# build the Qwik City frontend + SSR server.
#
# Gating: when CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY is unset (frontend-only deploys, preview
# environments, local re-runs) we still build the frontend but skip the
# backend push.

set -euo pipefail

if [ -n "${CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "==> Deploying Convex backend"
  # 1.46 fixes index-removal review with deploy-only keys. Keep CI deployment
  # tooling explicit even when the app's lockfile pins an older client.
  npx --yes convex@1.46.0 deploy --cmd 'bun run build.client && bun run build.server'
else
  echo "==> CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY not set — building frontend only, skipping convex deploy"
  bun run build.client
  bun run build.server
fi

{
  "$schema": "https://railway.com/railway.schema.json",
  "build": {
    "builder": "RAILPACK"

    "startCommand": "node server.js",
    "healthcheckPath": "/",
    "healthcheckTimeout": 120,
    "restartPolicyType": "ON_FAILURE",

  }
}

content.content:
== release.yml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
      - "twyne@*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.6"

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

      - name: Package release bundle
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-manual}"
          version="${version#twyne@}"
          mkdir -p release
          tar \
            --exclude="./node_modules" \
            --exclude="./release" \
            --exclude="./.git" \
            -czf "release/twyne-${version}.tar.gz" .

      - name: Publish GitHub release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: release/*.tar.gz
          generate_release_notes: true
          draft: false
          prerelease: false

  # Native desktop builds (Electrobun) — one runner per OS, each uploads its
  # app bundle to the same release the `release` job created. This is what the
  # landing page's "Download Twyne for desktop" link points at.
  desktop:
    needs: release
    name: Desktop (${{ matrix.label }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            label: macOS
            asset: twyne-desktop-macos
          - os: windows-latest
            label: Windows
            asset: twyne-desktop-windows
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            label: Linux
            asset: twyne-desktop-linux
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

# Changelog

## 0.27.0

<sub>2026-11-05</sub>

- Watch new words dry: what you type stays in a wetter blue-black ink until
  it is saved on this device, then dries to black. Ink that stays wet means
  the save has not landed.
- See where an action sends your words before you press it. Each destination
  has one ink, mark and word everywhere: this device, your account, your own
  model, hosted credit, or public.
- Hold to erase: deleting a comment, striking the room, removing a source,
  stopping sharing, removing a collaborator and unpublishing now ask you to
  hold the key, or press Enter twice, so a stray click cannot lose them.
- Choose how much the room moves in Preferences → Appearance → Motion: Full,
  Calm or Still, following your system by default. Your manuscript never
  moves at any level.
- Work under a desk lamp: a pool of light on the desk around the page, set by
  the hour and leaning toward your hand while you are not typing. Scrolling
  slides the paper under it.
- Keep your place in a long manuscript: the status bar names the section you
  are reading, and pressing it returns to that heading. It also says where
  your latest words are: held here, on the wire, or filed in your account.
- Watch an editor read: a pencil ring around their portrait follows the reply
  as it streams, new notes slip onto the board, and a new grade squeezes a
  little ink out from under the stamp.
- Move a section by its type slug onto a composing rule that names it, and
  see whether a dragged-in image will stay on this device or go to your
  account's storage.
- Open My Desk to figures set like type and bars that rise once. Patterns
  that reach their evidence are filed with a stamp, the selected range is
  marked again, and switching range no longer flashes the loader.
- Run a full analysis from the analysis page.
- Tidy the landing page's plates and guide.
